summary: Count to 100 by ones and tens, count on from any number, and write numerals 0 to 20.
Count objects one to one up to 20; the last number said tells how many.
Compare groups of objects and written numbers up to 10: greater, less or equal.
Build and break apart numbers 11 to 19 as ten ones and some more ones.
Add and subtract within 10: story problems, splitting numbers, making 10, fluency within 5.
Name flat and solid shapes in any size or position and describe where objects are.
Compare, build and draw shapes, and put small shapes together to make bigger ones.
Describe and directly compare objects by length, weight, area or capacity.
Sort objects into groups, count each group and compare the counts.
Count to 120 from any number and read and write numerals to 120.
Understand two-digit numbers as tens and ones and compare them with <, = and >.
Add within 100, find 10 more or less, and subtract multiples of 10 using place value.
Solve addition and subtraction story problems within 20 and add and subtract within 20 with strategies.
Use order and grouping properties to add, and see subtraction as a missing-addend problem.
Tell shapes apart by defining attributes and put flat or solid shapes together to make new ones.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths; more shares make smaller pieces.
Order objects by length, compare lengths indirectly, and measure by laying same-size units end to end.
Tell and write time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
Organize and read data in up to three categories and answer questions about it.
Understand three-digit numbers as hundreds, tens and ones and compare them with <, = and >.
Count within 1000, skip count by 5s, 10s and 100s, and read and write numbers to 1000.
Add and subtract within 1000 with place-value strategies and explain why the strategies work.
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction story problems within 100.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently using mental strategies.
Tell odd from even up to 20 and use repeated addition to count objects in arrays.
Recognize and draw shapes with given features such as number of angles or faces.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds and fourths; equal shares can look different.
Measure and estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters with suitable tools.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes on analog and digital clocks, with a.m. and p.m.
Solve money problems and make change with bills and coins, using $ and cent signs.
Show and read data with line plots, picture graphs and bar graphs.
Add and subtract lengths within 100 and show sums and differences on a number line.
Round to 10 or 100, add and subtract within 1000, and multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10.
Understand unit and other fractions, place them on a number line, and find equivalent fractions and compare.
Understand multiplication and division as equal groups and solve word problems within 100.
Use properties of multiplication and see division as a missing-factor problem.
Multiply and divide within 100 fluently and know all one-digit products from memory.
Solve two-step word problems with any operation and explain number patterns in tables.
Classify shapes by their attributes, such as quadrilaterals including rhombuses, rectangles and squares.
Split shapes into parts with equal area and name each part as a unit fraction.
Measure and estimate liquid volume, mass and length, and also solve problems about temperature.
Tell time to the minute and solve elapsed-time problems.
Count, compare and make change with coins and dollar bills (amounts under $5 on the state test).
Show and read data with tally charts, tables, pictographs, line plots and scaled bar graphs.
Find the area of rectangles by counting squares and link area to multiplication and addition.
Solve perimeter problems for polygons and tell perimeter apart from area.
Understand place value in multi-digit whole numbers; read, write, compare and round them.
Add and subtract multi-digit numbers fluently; multiply and divide using place value strategies.
Find equivalent fractions and compare fractions with different numerators and denominators.
Add and subtract like-denominator fractions and mixed numbers; multiply a fraction by a whole number.
Write tenths and hundredths as decimals, add tenths to hundredths, and compare decimals to hundredths.
Solve multiplicative comparison and multi-step word problems with all four operations.
Find factor pairs and multiples for numbers to 100 and tell prime from composite.
Make and describe number or shape patterns that follow one rule.
Draw and identify points, lines, rays, segments, angles, and parallel and perpendicular lines.
Sort two-dimensional figures by parallel or perpendicular sides and angle types.
Recognize symmetric figures and draw their lines of symmetry.
Convert larger units to smaller ones and solve measurement, money, area and perimeter problems.
Move data from one display to another, such as a table to a bar graph or pictograph.
Make line plots of fractional measurements and solve problems using them.
Measure and draw angles and find unknown angles by adding or subtracting adjacent angles.
Understand place value to thousandths, powers of ten, and read, write, compare and round decimals.
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers, divide by two-digit divisors, and compute with decimals to hundredths.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators using equivalent fractions.
Multiply fractions, see fractions as division, and divide unit fractions and whole numbers.
Write and evaluate numerical expressions with parentheses using the order of operations.
Make two number patterns from two rules, compare them and graph the ordered pairs.
Graph points in the first quadrant and use them to solve real-world problems.
Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on their properties.
Convert between units within one measurement system and use conversions in problems.
Show and read data in tallies, tables, pictographs, bar graphs and line graphs with a suitable scale.
Make line plots of fractional measurements and solve problems using fraction operations on them.
Understand volume, count unit cubes, and use multiplication and addition to find volumes of prisms.

state_code: # SOURCES (PA Core Standards for Mathematics, published in the Pennsylvania Bulletin March 1, 2014 as 22 Pa. Code ch. 4 Appendix A-2; still the current math standards per the State Board page checked 2026-10-01)

# - PDE text PDF of the same standards ("Academic Standards for Mathematics, Grades PreK-High School, March 1, 2014"), copy used for clean text: https://pryor.mathcs.wilkes.edu/mth303/PA%20Core%20Standards%20MTH%20(2014).pdf
# - SAS curriculum frameworks (Oct 2016, list the competencies under each standard): https://static.pdesas.org/content/documents/CF-Math_GRD_K_2016.pdf (also _1_, _2_, _3_, _4_, _5_)
# - SAS standards detail pages with eligible content, e.g. https://www.pdesas.org/standardsbrowse/0/161290 (CC.2.4.3.A.1), /162095 (CC.2.4.3.A.3)
# - No official PA Core-to-CCSS crosswalk for the final 2014 standards was found online (SAS links a 2012 crosswalk of the draft, no longer reachable). ccss mappings are my reading of the standard
#   statements (which reuse CCSS cluster headings) plus the curriculum-framework competencies (which are near-verbatim CCSS standards).
# - CC.2.<standard area>.<grade>.<strand letter>.<number>, e.g. CC.2.1.3.B.1; kindergarten is K (CC.2.1.K.A.1). "CC.2" = mathematics.
# - Each PA standard is a cluster-level statement (most are CCSS cluster headings), so one row usually covers several CCSS standards. There are no finer coded K-5 standards;
#   the finer PSSA Assessment Anchors / Eligible Content (e.g. M03.A-T.1.1.1) exist only for grades 3-8 and are assessment limits, not standards.
# - Numbering has gaps by design ("Intentionally Blank" cells), e.g. no CC.2.4.K.A.2/A.3, CC.2.4.1.A.3, CC.2.4.2.A.5, CC.2.1.3.B.2, CC.2.2.4.A.3, CC.2.2.5.A.2/A.3.
# - 2.1 Numbers and Operations: A = Counting and Cardinality (K), B = Numbers and Operations in Base Ten, C = Numbers and Operations - Fractions (3-5)
# - 2.2 Algebraic Concepts: A = Operations and Algebraic Thinking
# - 2.4 Measurement, Data, and Probability: A = Measurement and Data (A.1 measurement, A.2 time, A.3 money, A.4 data, A.5 area/volume, A.6 length operations/perimeter/angles)
# - Standards for Mathematical Practice are not coded and are skipped.
# CCSS K-5 STANDARDS DROPPED OR NOT FOUND
# - 2.G.A.2 (split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them): no grade 2 statement or framework competency covers it; CC.2.3.2.A.2 is only halves/thirds/fourths.
# - Every other CCSS K-5 standard is covered by the cluster-level statements.
# - Grade 3 money: CC.2.4.3.A.3 (count, compare, make change with coins and bills) - CCSS money is only 2.MD.C.8 and 4.MD.A.2.
# - Grade 3 data adds tally charts and tables (CC.2.4.3.A.4).
# - Grade 4: translating between data displays (CC.2.4.4.A.2). Grade 5: tallies, tables, pictographs, bar and line graphs with a scale (CC.2.4.5.A.2); CCSS 4-5 data is line plots only.
# - Grade 4 symmetry keeps its own standard (CC.2.3.4.A.3), same content as 4.G.A.3.
# - Statements are cluster-level, so ccss lists whole CCSS clusters. Where CCSS has more clusters than PA has statements, I assigned leftovers by fit:
#   1.OA.C (5, 6) and 1.OA.D.8 to CC.2.2.1.A.1 (the framework lists 1.OA.C.6 there); 1.OA.D.7 (equal sign) to CC.2.2.1.A.2.
# - K geometry: by statement wording K.G.A (identify/describe, incl. positions) -> CC.2.3.K.A.1 and K.G.B (analyze, compose) -> CC.2.3.K.A.2; the K framework instead lists
#   "compose larger shapes" under A.1 and "positions" under A.2.
# - 3.MD.B.4 (measure to half/quarter inch and line plot) is listed under both CC.2.4.3.A.1 (length) and CC.2.4.3.A.4 (line plots).
# - Grade 2 framework (2016) numbers the measurement standards differently from the 2014 standards (framework: A.2 time+money, A.3 data, A.4 length problems;
#   standards: A.2 time, A.3 money, A.4 data, A.6 length problems). This file follows the official 2014 standards.
# - CC.2.4.4.A.2 and CC.2.4.5.A.2 marked "moved" from 3.MD.B.3 (picture/bar graphs); they have no grade 4/5 CCSS counterpart. Grade 5 eligible content
#   M05.D-M.2.1.2 (SAS page https://www.pdesas.org/standardsbrowse/0/161317) adds line graphs, which CCSS K-5 lacks.
# - CC.2.4.3.A.4 marked edited (adds tally charts/tables); CC.2.4.K.A.1 kept same (area and capacity are just extra attribute examples).
